brief:
Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey dispatched senior security officials to Iran as concerns intensify over a potential renewed U.S.-Israeli military strike, Mondoweiss reported. The three nations have little influence over incoming U.S. policy toward Iran and face potentially severe consequences if armed conflict resumes.

Their rapid diplomatic engagement reflects alarm over the prospect of a conflict they say they cannot prevent. Gulf states hold minimal leverage to sway Trump administration decisions on military action against Iran.
dek: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Türkiye sent top security officials to Tehran as fears grow of a renewed U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran. With little leverage over Trump, the Gulf states face devastating consequences if the war resumes.
title: Gulf states rush envoys to Tehran as Iran war fears mount
